title: Travel, problems & emergencies
goal: Handle hotels, flights and money changing, report a loss or theft, get help in an emergency, and say 'if…, then…'.
intro:
Things go wrong on every trip: a cancelled flight, a lost bag, a landslide on the road. This unit gives you the language to deal with problems calmly — and to shout for help if you really need to.

The grammar point is the **conditional**. Nepali makes 'if' clauses with **भने** placed *after* the verb: पानी पर्‍यो **भने** 'if it rains'. You'll also learn the 'if only / would have' pattern for things that didn't happen.

vocab.note: A place to stay is also लज (lodge), गेस्ट हाउस.
मेरो फोन हरायो 'my phone got lost'; मैले फोन हराएँ 'I lost my phone'.

vocab.en: to go wrong, miss (the way); to make a mistake

vocab.note: In speech also पुलिस. Police post: प्रहरी चौकी.
आज बन्द छ 'there's a strike today'.

phrases.en: Do you have a room free?

phrases.native: यहाँ पैसा साट्ने ठाउँ कहाँ छ?
phrases.roman: yahāṃ paisā sāṭne ṭhāuṃ kahāṃ chha?
phrases.en: Where can I change money here?
There's no signal on my phone.
I need someone who speaks English.
I'm OK, nothing happened to me.

grammar.title: Real conditions: … भने …
grammar.body:
To say 'if X, (then) Y', put the X verb in the **simple past form** and add **भने** after it. The result clause comes second, in whatever tense makes sense:

पानी **पर्‍यो भने** म आउँदिनँ — 'If it rains, I won't come.'
तपाईं **आउनुभयो भने** हामी खुसी हुन्छौँ — 'If you come, we'll be happy.'

The past-form verb still agrees with its subject (म गएँ भने, ऊ गयो भने, तपाईं जानुभयो भने) — but it refers to the future. **यदि** 'if' can be added at the start for clarity: **यदि** पानी पर्‍यो **भने**…

A shorter form uses the ending **-ए** (no भने): पानी **परे** 'if it rains', पैसा **भए** 'if there's money', **नभए** 'if not / otherwise'.

Useful set phrases: **त्यसो भए** 'in that case, then', **नत्र** 'otherwise', **भए पनि** 'even if, although'.

examples.en: If you miss the bus, take a taxi.

examples.native: यदि झोला भेटियो भने हामी फोन गर्छौँ।
examples.roman: yadi jholā bheṭiyo bhane hāmi phon garchhauṃ.
examples.en: If the bag is found, we'll phone you.
If there's a problem, call me.
In that case, let's go tomorrow.
Even if it rains, we'll go.

grammar.title: Unreal conditions: 'if I had…, I would have…'
grammar.body:
For things that didn't happen, use **-एको भए** ('if (it) had been done') in the if-clause and **-ने थियो** ('would have') in the result:

थाहा **भएको भए** म **आउने थिएँ** — 'If I had known, I would have come.'

The थियो part conjugates for the person (थिएँ, थियौ, थियो, थिए, हुनुहुन्थ्यो). The same -ने थियो is used alone for 'would have / was going to': म त जाने थिएँ, तर… 'I was going to go, but…'.

A common lament: **…भइदिएको भए!** 'If only…!'

examples.native: तपाईंले भन्नुभएको भए म पर्खने थिएँ।
examples.roman: tapāiṃle bhannubhaeko bhae ma parkhane thieṃ.
examples.en: If you had told me, I would have waited.

examples.native: बाटो बन्द नभएको भए हामी पुग्ने थियौँ।
examples.roman: bāṭo banda nabhaeko bhae hāmi pugne thiyauṃ.
examples.en: If the road hadn't been closed, we would have arrived.

examples.native: म चाँडो उठेको भए उडान छुट्ने थिएन।
examples.roman: ma chāṃḍo uṭheko bhae uḍān chhuṭne thiena.
examples.en: If I had got up early, I wouldn't have missed the flight.

examples.native: मसँग पैसा भएको भए म किन्ने थिएँ।
examples.roman: masaṃga paisā bhaeko bhae ma kinne thieṃ.
examples.en: If I'd had the money, I would have bought it.

dialogue.title: The lost bag
dialogue.setting: Tom left his bag on a bus from Pokhara. He goes to the police post (प्रहरी चौकी) at the bus park.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: पोखराबाट आउने बसमा। मैले झोला सिटमुनि राखेको थिएँ।
lines.roman: Pokharābāṭa āune basmā. maile jholā siṭmuni rākheko thieṃ.
lines.en: On the bus from Pokhara. I had put the bag under the seat.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: मेरो पासपोर्ट, क्यामेरा र अलिकति पैसा।
lines.roman: mero pāsporṭ, kyāmerā ra alikati paisā.
lines.en: My passport, camera and some money.

lines.speaker: Police
lines.en: Do you know the bus number?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: थाहा छैन, तर मसँग टिकट छ।
lines.roman: thāhā chhaina, tara masaṃga ṭikaṭ chha.
lines.en: I don't know, but I have the ticket.

lines.speaker: Police
lines.native: राम्रो। टिकट छ भने हामी बस कम्पनीलाई फोन गर्न सक्छौँ।
lines.roman: rāmro. ṭikaṭ chha bhane hāmi bas kampanilāi phon garna sakchhauṃ.
lines.en: Good. If you have the ticket, we can phone the bus company.

lines.speaker: Police
lines.native: झोला भेटियो भने हामी फोन गर्छौँ। तपाईंको नम्बर लेखिदिनुहोस्।
lines.roman: jholā bheṭiyo bhane hāmi phon garchhauṃ. tapāiṃko nambar lekhidinuhos.
lines.en: If the bag is found, we'll call you. Please write down your number.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.en: And if it isn't found, what should I do?

lines.speaker: Police
lines.native: त्यसो भए पासपोर्टको लागि दूतावास जानुपर्छ। तर चिन्ता नगर्नुहोस्, प्रायः भेटिन्छ।
lines.roman: tyaso bhae pāsporṭko lāgi dutābās jānuparchha. tara chintā nagarnuhos, prāya bheṭinchha.
lines.en: Then you'll need to go to your embassy for a passport. But don't worry — it usually turns up.

culture: Emergency numbers in Nepal: **Police १००**, **Fire १०१**, **Ambulance १०२**, and the **Tourist Police ११४४** (in Kathmandu and Pokhara, with English speakers). In the mountains, rescue often means a helicopter, so trekkers should carry insurance that covers it. Road travel can be disrupted by landslides in the monsoon and occasionally by **बन्द** (political strikes), when shops close and vehicles stay off the roads. Nepal is generally safe and people are very helpful to travellers — lost items handed to a bus crew or police are often returned.
